description: RAIN reviews rural Nevada's clinical, telehealth, RPM, claims, transport, and SDOH systems overnight and surfaces maternal priority signals before you ask: elevated-risk pregnancies, prenatal care gaps, and emergency-delivery risk after the Battle Mountain obstetric closure.

Detects statistical outliers across cohorts and access metrics that no single rural system can identify — like the 6 high-risk patients whose missed visits, frontier ZIPs, and rising RPM blood-pressure trends only line up when the EHR, registry, claims, and RPM feed are read together.

Forecasts maternal risk escalation and recovery using cross-system longitudinal data — projecting how telehealth and hybrid interventions move prenatal completion from 61 percent back toward 88 percent and cut emergency-delivery risk.

Generates outreach lists, telehealth referrals, NEMT transport requests, cross-team handoffs, and board-ready briefs directly from the conversation — with the evidence chain from each contributing system assembled per patient.
